title: An operator's clear from the command line carries the operator's measured hand
intention: A clear made with cairn trouble clear carries the hand measured in the CLI's own process, and the trouble device passes it to clear(), so an operator's clear from their terminal closes the trouble at once and teaches the counting block.
why: Measured 2026-10-12: Akien ran ~/.akien/temp/clear-who-writes-what-2.sh from his own terminal (commons e1a7d39). All 9 who-writes-what troubles got a cleared_by entry by 'akien' with NO 'hand' key, so every one stayed OPEN and the counting block learned no row. Cause: cairn trouble clear (cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble, clear branch) asks over the bus (verb 'clear'), and TroubleDevice._handle_clear (cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py ~:193) calls self.clear(...) with no hand. c2172127d7a4 measured the hand only on the emission path (DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble), so the operator's own command never carried it and 1c1b18bac2eb's operator close never fired.
traces_to: Law 6 (the operator's gate: his clear must be his measured hand, not a typed name), and 1c1b18bac2eb / 0539e85f8b2d, which only work if the hand arrives.
how: Two sites in cairn/devices/trouble only. (a) 0/bin/trouble clear branch: before bus.request, measure hand = artifact.caller() (from cairn.tools.artifact import artifact), on exception {'class':'unknown','error':...} exactly as DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble does, and send it as body['hand']. (b) trouble.py _handle_clear: pass hand=body.get('hand') if isinstance(body.get('hand'), dict) else None to self.clear.
falsifier: cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py under PROVES {'63e6eb836769': {'1','2'}} on a scratch trouble store: (1) _handle_clear on an envelope whose body carries hand {'class':'akien'} closes an open trouble (standing CLEARED) and the entry carries that hand; (2) the CLI clear branch's body carries a 'hand' dict measured by artifact.caller() (asserted by running the branch's request-building against a fake bus and reading the body). Hollow: today's _handle_clear reds 1, today's CLI reds 2. Live, after PROVED: Akien re-runs ~/.akien/temp/clear-who-writes-what-2.sh and the 9 rows read CLEARED with hand class akien.
watchme: none, because the fault is measured at /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble and the proof's teeth are its falsifier
intent_berth: none, because this is a bug entering as a ticket (skills/intent/SKILL.md, the TICKET entry point), born from the measured fault at /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble

decisions.text: Measure in the CLI process and carry the result in the body, the same trust the emission path already gives a hand written in its file; the device does not re-measure, because in its process caller() would be the device itself. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
No backfill of the 9 hand-less entries already written: Akien re-runs his script after PROVED and the new entries carry the hand. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py stands written and measured red on today's code (2026-10-12: tooth 1 standing OPEN hand null; tooth 2 hand null), PROVES {'63e6eb836769': {'1': 'a_clear_verb_carrying_an_akien_hand_closes_the_trouble', '2': 'the_cli_clear_branch_sends_the_measured_hand'}}. Tooth 1 builds TroubleDevice(root=<scratch_dir store>), raises a trouble with recipients ['cc'], calls declared_verbs()['clear'] with body {identity, by 'akien', what_changed, hand {'class':'akien',...}} and asserts standing CLEARED and the last cleared_by hand equals that dict. Tooth 2 reads the bash clear) branch's python3 -c string out of cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble (unescaping \" and expanding $REPO_ROOT, the only two bash expansions it uses), execs it with a fake cairn.tools.bus_client whose reach() returns a bus recording request(**kw), and asserts body['hand'] is a dict whose class equals artifact.caller()['class'] measured in the same process. It is committed red before BUILDME; the build does not edit it. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The CLI edit, in cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble's clear) branch only: directly before 'bus = reach(...)' add 'from cairn.tools.artifact import artifact' then 'try:
    hand = artifact.caller()
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — the clear is the record; the hand is testimony
    hand = {'class': 'unknown', 'error': f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'}' (the same shape DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble uses at cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py:425-429, written with single quotes because the branch is a bash double-quoted string), preceded by a two-line comment citing c2172127d7a4 and 63e6eb836769; and add 'hand': hand to the request body dict. Nothing else in the file changes. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The device edit, in TroubleDevice._handle_clear (cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py:193) only: read hand = body.get('hand') and pass hand=hand if isinstance(hand, dict) else None to self.clear(...); one docstring sentence says the CLI's measured hand rides the body (63e6eb836769). clear() itself is unchanged: it already closes at once on an operator's hand (1c1b18bac2eb). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The voyage: commit the red proof (D3); cross TICKETME->BUILDME at cairn/devices/trouble (the component dir holding intention+why.json) through cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit(..., ticket='63e6eb836769', actor='cc', why=...), the returned cursor written onto the ticket through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(..., verb='cast'); build D4 (the CLI) and D5 (the device); run bin/cairn test cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py twice (green both times) and bin/cairn test cairn/devices/trouble/proofs (all green); commit; cross BUILDME->PROVEME with proven_by=['cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py']; bin/cairn test --seal cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_cli_clear_carries_the_hand.py; timeout 590 bin/cairn test --hollow 63e6eb836769 --seal, which reverts cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble (reds tooth 2) and cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py (reds tooth 1); verdict; push both repos; PROVED. The ticket names no trouble to clear and D2 holds: nothing is backfilled. After PROVED the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 is told by SendMessage so it can ask Akien to re-run his clear script. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof's test data is fixed in the committed file and the builder does not edit it: store = scratch_dir('cairn-proof-cli-clear-hand-') / 'store' (cairn.tools.scratch.scratch), TroubleDevice(root=str(store)) with set_diagnostic_receiver(None), raise_trouble('a-cli-clear-proof-trouble', why="a proof's trouble", detail={'n': 1}, recipients=['cc']), then the declared 'clear' verb with body {'identity': 'a-cli-clear-proof-trouble', 'by': 'akien', 'what_changed': 'the proof cleared it', 'hand': {'class': 'akien', 'unit': 'a-scope', 'ancestry': ['101:a-scope']}}; tooth 2 runs the CLI branch's Python with argv ['-c', 'a-cli-clear-proof-trouble', '--by', 'akien', '--what-changed', 'the proof cleared it'] against a fake bus_client.reach.
